propositions: Upper-bound wall-clock assertions in test files cause CI flake under runner contention and must be detected and blocked at code-review time

Tests with timing assertions can be escaped via either a reasoned '# timing: hang-guard — <reason>' line marker or the '@pytest.mark.skipif(CI == true)' perf-lane guard; bare '@pytest.mark.benchmark' alone does not escape

Two high-flake test sites (test_config_perf.py:201 and test_enrich_drain.py:261) must migrate to spy miss-path functions (cfg._ordered_layers for cache load; Q.pending_enrichment count for drain) rather than wall-clock bounds
Detector must integrate as a CI gate (wall-clock-assert step in _build-and-test.yml) with unit tests covering fire cases, both escape idioms, and lower-bound exclusion
Remaining nine in-scope test sites must carry reasoned hang-guard markers documenting why upper-bound assertions are safe (lock reclaim, subprocess/LLM timeouts, shutdown bounds, boot budget)
